skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. # TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm
2. 
3. Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.
4. 
5. ## Allowed `external_body`
6. 
7. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
8.   module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
9.   Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
10.   `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
11.   state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
12.   the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
13. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
14. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
15. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
16. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::new` — wraps a `FrameAddress` into an owning
17.   kernel-frame handle. Its body calls `crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page`, whose precondition is
18.   the **global** `identity_map_view().inv()`. That fact is owned by the `mm::virt` identity-map
19.   ghost token (a parameter-free singleton-global, like `phys_view()`), which is not realized in the
20.   `mm::phys` module and cannot be derived from the only available precondition (`base.inv()`). So
21.   the body cannot discharge the callee's `requires` in-scope. Same cross-module global-token
22.   deferral as `frame::book`/`frame::alloc` (post-mutation `phys_view()`): `external_body` until
23.   `mm::virt`'s identity-map token is realized, at which point `new` can pass it to
24.   `identity_map_page` and be verified in-body. `ensures Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@ && kf.inv()` (the
25.   address is preserved and page-aligned); `kframe`'s siblings `base`/`drop` verify in-body.
26. - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
27.   `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
28.   op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
29.   region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
30.   the abstract `bump_view`.
31. - `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
32.   `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
33.   `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.
34. 
35. ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
36. 
37. - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
38.   page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
39.   Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
40.   volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
41.   `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
42.   `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
43.   carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
44.   PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
45.   `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
46.   change).
47. - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
48.   page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
49.   Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
50.   `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
51.   `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
52.   index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
53.   contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
54.   `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
55.   `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
56.   slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
57.   **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
58.   `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.
59. 
60. ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging` (`mod.rs`)
61. 
62. - `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/mod.rs::invlpg` — the body is a single
63.   `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB
64.   entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be
65.   verified — an external-bottom hardware trust boundary (same class as the volatile
66.   page-table access in `table::read`/`write` and the int-to-pointer materialization in
67.   `frame::instance`/`bump_allocator::alloc`). See
68.   `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-mod/verus-unsupported.md`. The effect is purely on hardware TLB
69.   state (outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's Rust-visible state),
70.   so the faithful contract is **empty**: no `requires` (any `usize` is accepted), trivial
71.   `ensures` (returns `()`, no Rust-visible effect, every caller-side invariant preserved).
72.   This matches the inherited upstream
73.   `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs:151`
74.   `pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ](vaddr: usize);` (no
75.   `requires`/`ensures`). No exec signature changed.
76. 
77. ## Skip / exclude from current proof target
78. 
79. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
80. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`
81. 
82. ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `mm::phys`
83. 
84. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates an
85.   `alloc::collections::LinkedList` in a `for` loop. Verus has no `LinkedList` model and the
86.   orphan rule blocks providing one from the kernel crate (see
87.   `nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`). Body cannot be verified; `ensures` states that, on `Ok`,
88.   every frame in `phys_regions_frame_set(&physical_memory_regions)` becomes reserved.
89. - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same `LinkedList` limitation.
90.   `ensures` states that, on `Ok`, every *covered* frame in `mmio_regions_frame_set(mmio_regions)`
91.   becomes reserved (uncovered MMIO frames are skipped, matching the `frame::is_covered` gate).
92.
